andhra-pradesh: Southeastern coastal state with the Tirupati temple; new capital Amaravati
arunachal-pradesh: Northeasternmost state bordering China, the "land of the dawn-lit mountains"
assam: Northeastern state famous for its tea and one-horned rhinos
bihar: Eastern state where the Buddha found enlightenment at Bodh Gaya; capital Patna
chhattisgarh: Central state carved out in 2000, rich in forests and minerals; capital Raipur
goa: Smallest state, former Portuguese colony famous for beaches
gujarat: Western state, birthplace of Gandhi, with the Rann of Kutch
haryana: State around the capital region with Gurugram; shares a capital with its neighbour
himachal-pradesh: Himalayan state with Shimla and Manali
jharkhand: Mineral-rich eastern state formed in 2000; capital Ranchi
karnataka: Southern state with the tech hub Bengaluru and the ruins of Hampi
kerala: "God's own country": backwaters, spices and the city of Kochi
madhya-pradesh: The "heart of India", with Khajuraho temples; capital Bhopal
maharashtra: Western state with Mumbai and the Ajanta caves
manipur: Northeastern state where modern polo began; capital Imphal
meghalaya: "Abode of the clouds", one of the wettest places on Earth; capital Shillong
mizoram: Hilly northeastern state between Myanmar and Bangladesh; capital Aizawl
nagaland: Northeastern state known for the Hornbill Festival; capital Kohima
odisha: Eastern state with the Sun Temple at Konark and Puri's chariot festival
punjab: "Land of five rivers", home to the Golden Temple in Amritsar
rajasthan: Desert state of forts and palaces, with Jaipur, the "Pink City"
sikkim: Small Himalayan state beneath Kangchenjunga; capital Gangtok
tamil-nadu: Southern state with Chennai and towering temple gateways
telangana: India's newest state (2014), home to Hyderabad
tripura: Small northeastern state almost surrounded by Bangladesh; capital Agartala
uttar-pradesh: The most populous state, home to the Taj Mahal and Varanasi
uttarakhand: Himalayan state with Rishikesh and the source of the Ganges
west-bengal: Eastern state with Kolkata and Darjeeling tea
andaman-and-nicobar-islands: Island territory in the Bay of Bengal; capital Port Blair
chandigarh: Planned city by Le Corbusier, capital of two states
dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu: Merged western territory of former Portuguese enclaves
delhi: The national capital territory, home to India Gate and the Red Fort
jammu-and-kashmir: Himalayan territory with Srinagar's Dal Lake houseboats
ladakh: High-altitude desert territory with Leh and Pangong Lake
lakshadweep: Tiny coral island territory in the Arabian Sea
puducherry: Former French territory on the southeast coast
